purpose: Teach: 生殖/極度/入植/従属/太平洋戦争/払拭/多重/憎悪

lines.speaker: saito_doctor
lines.jp: 蓮さん、生殖医療を医療チームで丁寧に対応しております
lines.en: Ren — we handle reproductive medicine as a whole team, with real care and attention.
lines.style: Clear, steady opening. Professional but warm. Voice carries the weight of experience. No rush. Each phrase lands with quiet authority and genuine concern for the patient.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 極度のストレスを抱える患者さんに、貴院、ケアを提供されますね、先生
lines.en: Your hospital provides that kind of care even for patients carrying extreme stress, doesn't it? Doctor?
lines.style: Thoughtful pause before speaking. Genuine curiosity, not performative. Respectful of her expertise. Building toward something — careful, intelligent. A young man testing the depth of the conversation.

lines.speaker: saito_doctor
lines.jp: はい、戦後の入植者の心の傷を、医療チームで扱った経験があります
lines.en: Yes — we've had experience as a team handling the deep wounds that postwar survivors carry with them.
lines.style: Patient, unhurried. Weight of memory in the voice without sadness. Speaking from real cases, real people. Factual but human. The slight fatigue of someone who has carried this work for a long time.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 医療の従属関係を、貴院、解消されておられますね、先生
lines.en: So your hospital is working to change those unequal power dynamics in medicine, isn't it? Doctor?
lines.style: Slower, more intentional. He's moving into deeper territory now. Not challenging — genuinely seeking to understand her vision. Respect mixed with his own quiet intensity.

lines.speaker: saito_doctor
lines.jp: はい、太平洋戦争の負傷者の医療記録を医療チームで保存しております
lines.en: Yes — we preserve the medical records of the war injured from the Pacific War itself as a team, so we don't lose what happened.
lines.style: Measured, archival tone. Speaking of responsibility. Not burdened, but acknowledging the weight. Clear-eyed about history. The voice of someone who believes records matter because people matter.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 誤情報を払拭する啓発活動を、貴院、進めておられますね、先生
lines.en: And your hospital is pushing forward with education to clear away the misinformation that still surrounds all of this, isn't it? Doctor?
lines.style: Building momentum now. Still respectful, but his conviction is growing. He's putting the pieces together. Voice is firmer, more present. Asking because he already sees the pattern.

lines.speaker: saito_doctor
lines.jp: はい、多重感染症の対応を医療チームで備えております
lines.en: Yes — we prepare our team to handle complex, overlapping infections — it's part of comprehensive care.
lines.style: Pragmatic shift. Still patient but more direct. Speaking to present readiness, not just past work. Voice settles into the concrete. The physician moving from history to capability.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 医療への憎悪を抱える患者さんに、貴院、寄り添われますね、先生
lines.en: For patients who carry real hatred toward medicine itself — your hospital meets them with tenderness, doesn't it? Doctor?
lines.style: Slow, deliberate. This is his final question — the hardest one. Voice drops slightly. He's asking about the deepest work: healing distrust itself. Reverent without being flowery. Quiet conviction.
